Azad Jammu and Kashmir’s newly elected Prime Minister Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gillani called on his party’s leadership in Lahore on Sunday, with the latter stressing the need for the “immediate resolution” of issues of the Kashmiri people.
The huddle included PML-N President Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz and AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq, according to a post on the party’s X account.
During the meeting, Nawaz shared a “reform plan for the first 100 days” of Gillani’s tenure, the post said, adding that it was aimed at strengthening health, education, cleanliness, infrastructure and other sectors.
He instructed Gillani to set AJK on the course of development, similar to Punjab, it said.
Gillani and Farooq expressed gratitude to the party’s senior leadership for “their confidence” in him, while the latter congratulated Gillani and Farooq.
A day earlier, the AJK PM had assured the business community and students that his government would restore internet services at educational institutions and remove restrictions on road links with Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa within the next few days.
PM Gillani had also expressed concern over the situation in Rawalakot, saying his government would make every effort to bring it under control.
AJK has been gripped by protests, including in Rawalakot, staged by the now-proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee that had announced a boycott of the recently held elections in the region over its demand for abolishing 12 seats reserved in the assembly for families displaced from occupied Kashmir.
The protests have been marred by violence while AJK continues to face internet disruptions.
Against this backdrop, the elections in the region, originally scheduled for July 27, were divided into phases over security concerns amid unrest in the region. The first phase was held on July 27, the second on Aug 2 and the third on Aug 10.
Meanwhile, the third phase was originally meant to cover all of Poonch Division, which comprises 11 constituencies, including three in Bagh, one in Haveli, five in Poonch district and two in Sudhnoti district.
However, the AJK Election Commission announced that polling would only go ahead as scheduled in Bagh and Haveli because of concerns over the law and order situation.

deduped_items.summary: ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority has sealed three buildings in the city’s commercial hub for failing to comply with fire safety regulations, officials said Monday. The Shaheed-e-Millat Secretariat, State Life Building and Trade Development Authority of Pakistan Building in Blue Area were shut down after inspections revealed unresolved safety deficiencies, according to the CDA’s Fire ... Read more The post CDA seals 3 Islamabad buildings over fire safety violations appeared first on B
deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Capital Development Authority has sealed three buildings in the city’s commercial hub for failing to comply with fire safety regulations, officials said Monday.
The Shaheed-e-Millat Secretariat, State Life Building and Trade Development Authority of Pakistan Building in Blue Area were shut down after inspections revealed unresolved safety deficiencies, according to the CDA’s Fire & Emergency Services Directorate.
CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf ordered the enforcement action and directed authorities to adopt a zero-tolerance approach toward fire safety violations.
“No building, institution or organization can be permitted to compromise the lives and safety of people by ignoring essential fire prevention and emergency response requirements,” Ashraf said in a statement.
The fire safety directorate has been conducting building inspections across Islamabad to identify violations related to emergency exits, firefighting equipment, evacuation plans and other life-safety measures.
The CDA’s Building Control Section has been instructed to give building administrations a prescribed timeframe to correct deficiencies.
Officials said the enforcement drive is not merely an inspection exercise but a practical initiative aimed at preventing avoidable loss of life and property.
Ashraf directed relevant departments to maintain close monitoring of compliance and ensure that safety observations are followed by corrective measures.
The CDA urged all government departments, public sector organizations, commercial establishments and private building owners to review their fire safety arrangements immediately.
“Fire safety is a collective responsibility,” Ashraf said. “Timely installation and maintenance of firefighting equipment, clear emergency exits, proper evacuation arrangements and compliance with safety protocols can save lives during an emergency.”
The authority said it would provide opportunities for building administrations to rectify deficiencies but warned that continued noncompliance would not be tolerated.
“Protection of human lives is the first and foremost responsibility,” the CDA said. “No compromise will be made on fire and life safety.”

CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf ordered the enforcement action and directed authorities to adopt a zero-tolerance approach toward fire safety violations.
“No building, institution or organization can be permitted to compromise the lives and safety of people by ignoring essential fire prevention and emergency response requirements,” Ashraf said in a statement.
The fire safety directorate has been conducting building inspections across Islamabad to identify violations related to emergency exits, firefighting equipment, evacuation plans and other life-safety measures.
The CDA’s Building Control Section has been instructed to give building administrations a prescribed timeframe to correct deficiencies.
Officials said the enforcement drive is not merely an inspection exercise but a practical initiative aimed at preventing avoidable loss of life and property.
Ashraf directed relevant departments to maintain close monitoring of compliance and ensure that safety observations are followed by corrective measures.
The CDA urged all government departments, public sector organizations, commercial establishments and private building owners to review their fire safety arrangements immediately.
“Fire safety is a collective responsibility,” Ashraf said. “Timely installation and maintenance of firefighting equipment, clear emergency exits, proper evacuation arrangements and compliance with safety protocols can save lives during an emergency.”
The authority said it would provide opportunities for building administrations to rectify deficiencies but warned that continued noncompliance would not be tolerated.

deduped_items.title: New intellectual biography explores life and legacy of Iraqi sociologist Ali Al Wardi
deduped_items.summary: Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A new intellectual biography examining the life and critical scholarship of Iraq’s founding father of sociology, Ali Al-Wardi, has been released by the American University of Iraq, […] The post New intellectual biography explores life and legacy of Iraqi sociologist Ali Al Wardi appeared first on Iraqi News.
deduped_items.body_text:
New intellectual biography explores life and legacy of Iraqi sociologist Ali Al Wardi
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A new intellectual biography examining the life and critical scholarship of Iraq’s founding father of sociology, Ali Al-Wardi, has been released by the American University of Iraq, Baghdad (AUIB) Press.
Authored by Iraqi philosopher and translator Ali Hakim Saleh, the 300-page volume—titled Ali Al-Wardi: An Intellectual and Social Biography — traces Al-Wardi’s transformation into an urban modern intellectual (effendi), his systemic deconstruction of official state narratives, and the subsequent censorship and institutional marginalization he faced.
The biography structures Al-Wardi’s life and academic legacy across several defining phases:
- The Rise of the “Effendi” and the Public Intellectual: Tracing Al-Wardi’s emergence from traditional quarters to Western academia (earning his Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin in 1950) and his creation of a broad reading public outside elite scholarly circles.
- Theorizing the Iraqi Persona: Examining his foundational sociological frameworks, notably the dialectic between nomadism (Badawa) and urban civilization (Hadara), and the concept of psychological duality (Izdawajiyya) within Iraqi society.
- Direct Critique of Political Power: Analyzing Al-Wardi’s rigorous critique of state structures and his disruption of official historiography, most prominently captured in his multi-volume opus, Social Glimpses from Modern Iraqi History.
- State Friction, Censorship, and Disillusionment: Documenting the political suppression, academic sidelining, and personal disillusionment that followed his confrontation with authoritarian state narratives.
The publication has generated significant interest across Iraqi cultural and academic circles. Prominent author and University of Basra professor Louay Hamza Abbas praised the work as a major cultural milestone:
“The release of this book is a distinguished cultural event… not merely because it is the first comprehensive socio-intellectual biography of the father of Iraqi sociology, but for deeper considerations: No thinker remains from modern Iraqi culture to whom we return whenever calamity strikes us other than Ali Al-Wardi. They have all departed.”

Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A new intellectual biography examining the life and critical scholarship of Iraq’s founding father of sociology, Ali Al-Wardi, has been released by the American University of Iraq, Baghdad (AUIB) Press.
Authored by Iraqi philosopher and translator Ali Hakim Saleh, the 300-page volume—titled Ali Al-Wardi: An Intellectual and Social Biography — traces Al-Wardi’s transformation into an urban modern intellectual (effendi), his systemic deconstruction of official state narratives, and the subsequent censorship and institutional marginalization he faced.
The biography structures Al-Wardi’s life and academic legacy across several defining phases:
- The Rise of the “Effendi” and the Public Intellectual: Tracing Al-Wardi’s emergence from traditional quarters to Western academia (earning his Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin in 1950) and his creation of a broad reading public outside elite scholarly circles.
- Theorizing the Iraqi Persona: Examining his foundational sociological frameworks, notably the dialectic between nomadism (Badawa) and urban civilization (Hadara), and the concept of psychological duality (Izdawajiyya) within Iraqi society.
- Direct Critique of Political Power: Analyzing Al-Wardi’s rigorous critique of state structures and his disruption of official historiography, most prominently captured in his multi-volume opus, Social Glimpses from Modern Iraqi History.
- State Friction, Censorship, and Disillusionment: Documenting the political suppression, academic sidelining, and personal disillusionment that followed his confrontation with authoritarian state narratives.
The publication has generated significant interest across Iraqi cultural and academic circles. Prominent author and University of Basra professor Louay Hamza Abbas praised the work as a major cultural milestone:
“The release of this book is a distinguished cultural event… not merely because it is the first comprehensive socio-intellectual biography of the father of Iraqi sociology, but for deeper considerations: No thinker remains from modern Iraqi culture to whom we return whenever calamity strikes us other than Ali Al-Wardi. They have all departed.”

Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council          
        Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here.
Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.
US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed.
Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty.
Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise.
Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days.
In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar.
Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment.
On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro.
Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain.
Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks.
RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda.
Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr.
And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations.
Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary.

Warraq residents demonstrate to protest ‘state ignoring legitimate demands’          
        Hundreds of Warraq Island residents held a protest march on Tuesday, after the head of the authority tasked with developing the island failed to respond to demands they submitted last week, one of the participants in the march told Mada Masr.
Hundreds of residents gathered in the street on Tuesday morning, on the deadline they had given authorities to respond to demands they submitted last week, including that they be granted lands within the state development project, according to the participant as well as videos published by other residents who attended the march.
The crowd then marched toward the New Warraq City Development headquarters, where a heavy security deployment awaited them. Security officials told them that the head of the authority asked for a small group to enter for negotiations.
The protestors refused, instead demanding that the authority’s head come down to meet them, in an attempt to get a direct response to the demands they had already submitted in writing.
The resident who took part in Tuesday’s march said the authority head’s refusal to come down and meet the residents sparked anger among many of them, but that they kept it in check out of their keenness to keep the protest peaceful.
But it showed “a lack of consideration, especially since he didn’t meet us when we came to hand over the demands,” the resident said.
The same sentiment was clear at the protest. “Nobody has paid us any attention,” one of the protesters called out to the assembled crowd. “At this moment, we register our objection to the state’s disregard for our legitimate and just demands by saying just one thing: God is sufficient for us, and he is the best disposer of all affairs,” indicating the group’s loss of faith in the authorities’ seriousness.
The residents then continued their peaceful protest march along the route that had been agreed to in advance. While the march had been planned without chants, still, the residents raised similar cries of “God is sufficient for us” and “one hand.”
At the end of the march, the residents agreed to meet again on Friday to discuss their next steps, and raised the possibility of disrupting ongoing development work on the island.
The residents had submitted a list of demands to the authority on August 18, foremost among them that they be allocated a plot of land within the island’s redevelopment area, where residents who have chosen to stay could build their own homes, according to a defined timeline, with clear and specific implementation mechanisms and fair conditions. They also put forward other demands concerning living and security conditions on the island.
The group handed their written demands to the authority’s deputy chair at the time, with the head elsewhere with another group of Warraq residents, inspecting one of the island’s schools, supposedly to assess potential upgrades.
The resident described to Mada Masr the authority head’s meeting with that group as part of security attempts to “divide.”
One of the people in the group that did not join Tuesday’s march said there were some who had not attended the recent meeting that produced the list of demands. The group who went with the authority head on his school visit opposes holding marches to the authority’s offices, they told Mada Masr. Instead, they have been trying to communicate with officials at the authority and pressure them to implement “as many things as possible that would allow us to keep living on the island,” they continued, adding that they are convinced the government would not agree to give residents land on the island to replace their homes.
The source pointed to what they saw as officials responding to some of the residents’ service-related demands, including bringing back sewage pumping trucks and beginning to clear demolition waste that had piled up along the island’s roads.

Sudan Nashra: Military strikes RSF convoy inside Chadian territory, sparks regional concerns | Kauda fighting pushes Otoro groups to demand Hilu’s removal from SPLM-N leadership | US proposes nationwide arms embargo on Sudan in Security Council          
        Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter here.
Washington is pushing in the United Nations Security Council to take the Darfur arms embargo nationwide.
US Senior Advisor on Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos put the proposal on the table on Monday, after first floating the idea at a council session in June. The draft would expand the 2005 Darfur sanctions regime to all of Sudan, while explicitly bringing drones and related technology under the embargo. The current regime expires in September unless amended or renewed.
Boulos pointed to the growing toll from drone warfare, saying drones accounted for nearly 80 percent of casualties this year and that both sides continue to strike civilians and civilian infrastructure.
Khartoum rejected the proposal outright. Sudan’s ambassador to the UN Al-Harith Idriss said applying the same restrictions nationwide would amount to equating “the state institutions and the rebel militia,” calling the proposal an attack on Sudan’s sovereignty.
Washington has to get past Russia and China, which both pushed back against expanding the sanctions regime and can veto any council resolution. So while the proposal has support from some council members, it is unlikely to go anywhere without a compromise.
Sudan’s drone war crossed its borders twice over the past days.
In western Sudan, military drones struck a convoy of hundreds of Rapid Support Forces vehicles on August 20 inside Chad’s eastern Ennedi region, near the Sudanese border. Two Sudanese military sources said the convoy had been assembled over several weeks at camps in southeastern Libya, and was preparing to enter Darfur through Chad using a new route through North Darfur’s Wadi Howar.
Chad condemned the strike as a violation of its sovereignty and warned that it reserved the right to respond, prompting the African Union to call for restraint and dialogue to prevent a regional escalation. The Sudanese military has yet to comment.
On the other side of the country, the military said a strategic drone crossed into Blue Nile State from Ethiopian territory and was shot down over Dindro.
Inside the RSF camp, its main ally in the war and its parallel government, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, led by Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, continues to grapple with an internal crisis that is becoming harder to contain.
Fighting with one of its oldest constituencies, the Otoro tribe, has returned to Kauda, the movement’s political and military center in South Kordofan, with control shifting between the two sides over the past two weeks.
RSF commander Mohamed Hamdan “Hemedti” Dagalo intervened and called for a ceasefire, but overlapping control on the ground made that impossible to sustain. The ceasefire collapsed, and Otoro fighters regained the upper hand in Kauda.
Some Otoro groups are now calling for Hilu to step down and are seeking alliances with other Nuba Mountains constituencies to challenge a political order that the SPLM-N has dominated for decades, but which has increasingly been concentrated in a narrow circle around Hilu, two Otoro leaders told Mada Masr.
And while there is still no end in sight to the war’s battles, Khartoum is preparing to use September’s UN General Assembly in New York to consolidate a post-Khartoum political posture and present its vision for Sudan’s political and institutional order after the war, according to Sudanese diplomatic and government sources informed of the preparations.
Transitional Sovereignty Council Chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan remains the leading option to head the delegation. But US sanctions imposed on him in 2025 could make his participation complicated, prompting the government to consider other senior officials if necessary.

deduped_items.title: Egypt issues 907 livestock licenses and injects EGP59.850m into National Veal Project in August
deduped_items.summary: Egypt’s Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation issued 907 operating licenses for livestock, poultry, feed, and dairy collection projects in August, whilst approving EGP 59.850m in new financing for the National Veal Project. The figures were detailed in an official August report submitted to Minister of Agriculture Alaa Farouk by Tarek Soliman, head of […] The post Egypt issues 907 livestock licenses and injects EGP59.850m into National Veal Project in August first appeared on Dailynewsegy
deduped_items.body_text:
Egypt’s Ministry of Agriculture and Land Reclamation issued 907 operating licenses for livestock, poultry, feed, and dairy collection projects in August, whilst approving EGP 59.850m in new financing for the National Veal Project.
The figures were detailed in an official August report submitted to Minister of Agriculture Alaa Farouk by Tarek Soliman, head of the livestock and poultry development sector.
Soliman stated that the new Veal Project financing will support 47 beneficiaries raising 855 head of cattle. This brings the total funding granted since the project’s inception to over EGP 11.514bn, benefiting 46,398 small breeders, graduates, and women across “Decent Life” initiative villages, and covering more than 543,417 head of cattle.
Of the 907 operating licenses issued during the month, 167 were permits granted to small breeders for livestock rearing, coordinated with the General Authority for Veterinary Services. The ministry also granted 28 technical approvals for new animal and poultry production projects in desert hinterland areas to enforce biosecurity requirements and distance major production activities from residential blocks.
In addition to licensing, the sector supervised the destruction of a shipment of non-compliant imported feed additives totalling 2,304 tonnes and 1,200 litres via joint inspection committees. Soliman noted that the ministry continued surprise inspection campaigns on factories and warehouses across governorates to confront monopolies and the withholding of goods.
The ministry approved 777 registrations for feed mixtures, additives, and concentrates, comprising 416 local and 361 imported registrations. This was conducted in cooperation with the Regional Center for Food and Feed and the Animal Production Research Institute. Soliman stated that the oversight and registration aim to reduce production costs and improve food conversion rates and final product quality.
Technical support and homogeneity tests were also provided for 47 feed factories, encompassing 106 production lines dedicated to poultry, livestock, and fish, in preparation for their licensing. The ministry, overseen by Deputy Minister Mostafa Al-Sayyad, organised eight extension seminars and practical training sessions in several governorates to transfer modern feeding and care practices to breeders.
Soliman added that during August, Egypt exported quantities of fish feed, feed additives, frozen poultry, table eggs, and frozen birds—including quail, duck, pigeon, and turkey—to several Arab and foreign markets.

deduped_items.title: "Only ashes and bones left": what we know about those killed in the Russian strike on Bucha ammunition depots
deduped_items.summary: Thirty-eight people were killed when a Russian drone strike triggered the detonation of ammunition in the village of Myla, in the Bucha district near Kyiv. Among them were Valentyna, who lived at the Dobryi Dim care home for the elderly, and 52-year-old local resident Vitalii Momot.

deduped_items.title: EU Officials Deny Imminent Russian Threat to NATO Despite CIA Visit

deduped_items.title: Мартинес перешел из «Астон Виллы» в «Челси»
deduped_items.body_text:
Вратарь сборной Аргентины Эмилиано Мартинес перешел из «Астон Виллы» в «Челси», подписав трехлетний контракт с лондонским клубом. Об этом объявила пресс-служба «Челси».
По данным журналиста Фабрицио Романо, сумма трансфера составила 7,5 миллиона фунтов (8,7 миллиона евро). Мартинес может дебютировать за новый клуб уже 30 августа во втором туре АПЛ против «Брайтона».
«Я рад оказаться в этом футбольном клубе. Переход в «Челси» был простым решением для меня и моей семьи, и я просто невероятно счастлив — не могу дождаться начала работы», — заявил голкипер.
По информации The Guardian, Мартинес получал и другие предложения, но выразил желание играть под руководством главного тренера «Челси» Хаби Алонсо.
За «Астон Виллу» аргентинец выступал с 2020 года и провел 256 матчей за шесть сезонов. В мае он стал победителем Лиги Европы. Вместе со сборной Аргентины Мартинес выиграл чемпионат мира 2022 года и Кубок Америки в 2021-м и 2024-м. В 2023-м и 2024-м голкипер получал приз имени Льва Яшина как лучший вратарь года.

deduped_items.title: Природному пожару в Анапе присвоили повышенную категорию сложности
deduped_items.body_text:
Природному пожару в Анапе присвоили третий, повышенный ранг сложности. Об этом объявили в пресс-службе МЧС по региону, пишет агентство РИА Новости.
«Пожару присвоен повышенный ранг сложности номер три», — сказано в сообщении. Отмечается, что в его тушении задействованы 43 спасателя и 14 единиц техники.
Пожар вспыхнул днем в воскресенье, 30 августа, в плавнях Анапы в районе Чембурки и охватил площадь около 10 гектаров, рассказала глава города-курорта Светлана Маслова. Из-за возгорания пришлось ограничить движение по федеральной трассе.
Ранее стало известно, что во Франции ухудшилось качество воздуха из-за лесных пожаров.

deduped_items.title: Врач оценила правдивость утверждения о связи кофе и высокого давления
deduped_items.body_text:
Влияние кофе на артериальное давление не так однозначно, как принято думать, заявила кардиолог сети клиник «Семейная» Наталья Соловьева. Правдивость утверждения о связи кофе и гипертонии она оценила в разговоре с «Лентой.ру».
«Сразу после выпитой чашки кофе артериальное давление действительно повышается. Однако этот показатель, как правило, меняется незначительно и самостоятельно возвращается к норме в течение пары часов. Также стоит отметить, что при регулярном употреблении кофе на протяжении длительного времени этот эффект исчезает. Организм адаптируется к постоянной стимуляции, и напиток больше не влияет на давление», — рассказала Соловьева.
Врач подчеркнула: на тему влияния кофе на артериальное давление проведено много исследований. Их результаты показали, что стойкого повышения этого показателя не было зафиксировано ни в молодом возрасте, ни у людей старшей возрастной группы. Более того, часть исследователей отметили парадоксальное снижение уровня артериального давления при длительном употреблении умеренного количества кофе, отметила кардиолог.
Она добавила, что безопасным количеством считается до 400 граммов кофеина в день. Это эквивалентно трем-четырем чашкам эспрессо.
Ранее онколог Владимир Ивашков рассказал, что здоровье мозга может незаметно разрушать гипертония. Он объяснил, что высокое давление разрушает сосуды во всем организме, вызывая со временем тяжелые поражения.

deduped_items.title: В Индии назвали самые популярные маршруты на Гоа
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Понда, Ривона и Нетравали — популярные маршруты на Гоа для любителей активного и познавательного отдыха, где сосредоточены исторические достопримечательности и природные объекты.
- На маршруте Старый Гоа — Дивар — Чорао — Кумбарджуа можно увидеть исторические церкви и памятники, паромные переправы, островные деревни и мангровые заросли.
- Маршрут Канакона — Кепем — Кабо-де-Рама подойдет туристам, предпочитающим тихие пляжи, прибрежные деревни, живописные дороги и заповедники дикой природы.
МОСКВА, 30 авг - РИА Новости. Наиболее популярными маршрутами на Гоа в Индии для любителей активного и познавательного отдыха являются Понда, Ривона и Нетравали, здесь сосредоточены исторические храмы, святые места, древние пещеры, плантации специй, леса и водопады, рассказал РИА Новости глава департамента туризма штата Кедар Наик. 
 Исторические церкви и памятники, паромные переправы, островные деревни, мангровые заросли можно увидеть на маршруте Старый Гоа — Дивар — Чорао — Кумбарджуа, добавил он. 
Россияне стали чаще ездить в Индию на йога-ретриты
22 августа, 04:28
Туристам, предпочитающим тихие пляжи, прибрежные деревни, живописные дороги и заповедники дикой природы, подойдет, по его словам, маршрут Канакона — Кепем — Кабо-де-Рама. 
В ведомстве также рекомендовали обратить внимание на форт Рейш-Магуш, традиционные исторические дома, высеченные в скалах пещеры и плантации специй. 
"Эти маршруты особенно подходят путешественникам, предпочитающим длинные поездки, неспешный темп и индивидуально составленные программы вдали от переполненных туристических зон", - сказал собеседник агентства.

deduped_items.title: Эксперт рассказал, что России дает статус крупной экономики
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Россия по итогам прошлого года стала четвертой экономикой мира с ВВП более 7 триллионов долларов по паритету покупательной способности.
- Статус крупной экономики позволяет России увереннее переживать внешние шоки, так как значительная часть спроса и финансирования формируется внутри страны.
- Крупный внутренний рынок дает национальным компаниям возможность расти в более понятной среде и выходить на внешние рынки с более сильной конкурентной позицией.
МОСКВА, 30 авг - РИА Новости. Статус крупной экономики позволяет России увереннее переживать внешние шоки и обеспечивает национальным компаниям более понятную среду для ведения бизнеса, заявил РИА Новости ведущий аналитик по суверенным и региональным рейтингам агентства "Эксперт РА" Кирилл Лысенко. 
Аналитик оценил, когда ждать рывка российской экономики
26 августа, 15:33
"Крупная экономика обычно лучше держится в реалиях внешних шоков, поскольку значительная часть спроса и финансирования формируется внутри страны", - ответил эксперт на вопрос, что дает России ее статус одной из крупнейших экономик мира. 
Это снижает зависимость от состояния отдельных внешних рынков и дает больше возможностей компенсировать ухудшение внешней конъюнктуры внутренними источниками роста, пояснил Лысенко. 
"Крупный внутренний рынок дает национальным компаниям возможность сначала расти в более понятной для них среде – с известным потребителем, знакомым регулированием, устойчивыми каналами сбыта и без дополнительных издержек, связанных с выходом за рубеж. Это позволяет набрать масштаб, накопить производственный опыт, улучшить продукт и снизить издержки, а уже затем выходить на более агрессивные внешние рынки с более сильной конкурентной позицией", - добавил он. 
При этом аналитик напомнил, что пока Россию от тройки лидеров отделяет большой разрыв. Российская экономика, по словам эксперта, примерно в 2,4 раза меньше индийской, более чем в 4 раза меньше американской и почти в 6 раз меньше китайской. Главным претендентом на четвертое место, по его мнению, сейчас является Индонезия.
Аналитик оценил вхождение России в число крупнейших экономик мира
26 августа, 10:34

deduped_items.title: В очереди перед Крымским мостом скопилось более 600 машин
deduped_items.body_text:
Краткий пересказ от РИА ИИ
- Свыше 600 машин скопилось перед Крымским мостом, время ожидания составляет около часа.
- В очереди на ручной досмотр со стороны Тамани находятся 350 транспортных средств, со стороны Керчи — 300 машин.
СИМФЕРОПОЛЬ, 30 авг - РИА Новости. Свыше 600 машин скопилось перед Крымским мостом, время ожидания составляет около часа, сообщается в канале инфоцентра о ситуации на автоподходах к мосту. 
Статистика приведена по состоянию на 15.00 мск. 
При этом в очереди со стороны Керчи стоят 300 машин. Там время ожидания также составляет около часа. 
Проезд по Крымскому мосту разрешен легковым автомобилям, микроавтобусам и автобусам. Грузовой транспорт следует в Крым по маршруту через новые регионы. Перед въездом на мост с двух сторон для обеспечения безопасного движения установлены посты досмотра.

deduped_items.body_text:
Mansilla de las Mulas (León) exhibe en su Feria del Tomate un producción «abundante y de muy buena calidad y sabor»
La recolección de este año alcanza los 300.000 kilos
León
Mansilla de las Mulas (León) celebra este domingo la jornada central de su XXXVII Feria del Tomate, que congrega a numerosos asistentes en el entorno de la Plaza del Grano de la localidad, donde se instalan los puntos de venta del preciado producto, en una ... cita que premia los mejores ejemplares entre las muestras recogidas en los expositores.
Este año la producción se considera «muy buena, abundante, de muy buena calidad y sabor, con un tomate muy limpio y de buen tamaño», según explicó a la agencia Ical el presidente de la Promotora de la Indicación Geográfica Protegida del Tomate de Mansilla de las Mulas, José Miguel Olmo, quien señaló que el intenso calor vivido durante varias jornadas no perjudicó la evolución del cultivo; más bien contribuyó a aumentar el tamaño de las piezas. Además expresó su confianza en que las frescas jornadas vividas en días pasados tampoco causen problemas.
Noticia relacionada
Sin querer aventurar cifras concretas, la producción de este año se considera similar a la de otras campañas sin sobresaltos, con unos 300.000 kilogramos recolectados entre los integrantes de la cooperativa y una veintena de agricultores profesionales que tienen en el tomate uno de sus principales cultivos, aunque los datos ofrecidos en alguna ocasión superaron ampliamente los 400.000.
Respecto al proceso para la obtención de la Indicación Geográfica Protegida (IGP) para el tomate de Mansilla, iniciado hace ya un lustro, el presidente de la Promotora reconoce una vez más que el asunto «sigue parado de momento». «Seguimos con el objetivo» asegura al tiempo que detalla que no se ha remitido nueva documentación no realizado más gestiones al respecto desde entonces.
La Feria del Tomate de Mansilla, inaugurada a mediodía, contó también con una nutrida representación institucional, con la presencia entre otras autoridades y cargos institucionales y políticos del vicepresidente primero y consejero de Desregulación, Familia y Ayudas Sociales, Carlos Pollán, el subdelegado del Gobierno en León, Héctor Alaiz, la secretaria general de la Unión del Pueblo Leonés, Alicia García, la vicesecretaria general del Partido Socialista de Castilla y León, Nuria Rubio, el diputado de Turismo, Octavio González o el líder provincial del PSOE, Javier Alfonso Cendón, quienes arroparon a la alcaldesa de Mansilla, Vicenta García, y tuvieron ocasión de recorrer los puestos instalados, comprobar la calidad y sabor de los tomates e incluso comprarlos, en algún caso.

deduped_items.body_text:
Productores ecológicos piden usar forrajes convencionales de forma «puntual» por la sequía
Proecogal reclama a las administraciones mecanismos excepcionales para garantizar la alimentación del ganado y evitar que se agoten las reservas de las explotaciones
ABC
Santiago
La Asociación de Productores de Ecolóxico de Galicia (Proecogal) ha reclamado «medidas urgentes» para hacer frente a los efectos de la sequía y de las elevadas temperaturas en las explotaciones de este tipo. Entre las sugeridas, citan la posibilidad de autorizar temporalmente el uso de ... hierba seca o forrajes convencionales de proximidad para paliar la pérdida de alimento ecológico causada.
A través de un comunicado, recogido por EP, la asociación explica que la falta de pastos y forrajes está provocando que las reservas destinadas para el invierno se estén agotando. Esto, según expone, está obligando a las explotaciones a acudir antes de lo previsto al mercado para garantizar la alimentación del ganado, «en un contexto de escasez e incremento de los precios generalizado».
Por ello, Proecogal considera «imprescindible» que las administraciones «actúen ya» y articulen «mecanismos excepcionales para una situación excepcional». En ello, incluyen la posibilidad de autorizar temporalmente el uso de hierba seca o forrajes convencionales de proximidad en las explotaciones afectadas por la carencia de alimento ecológico.
Precisa que esto se trataría de un uso «muy reducido y puntual» de alimento convencional, «limitado a las circunstancias excepcionales actuales y siempre dentro del marco de la normativa europea», incide. Esta tendría el objetivo de garantizar la alimentación de los animales y la continuidad de las explotaciones.
La asociación ya ha mantenido una reunión con el Consejo Regulador de la Agricultura Ecológica de Galicia (Craega) para trasladar directamente la problemática que están viviendo los productores. A su vez, el organismo remitió la cuestión a la Axencia Galega de Calidade Alimentaria (Agacal), adscrita a la Consellería do Medio Rural. De este modo, Proecogal considera «fundamental» que los dos entes actúen «coordinadamente» para buscar una solución.
«Desde Proecogal estamos llamando a todas las puertas que tienen responsabilidad para defender los intereses de nuestros asociados y, en general, de los productores y productoras del sector ecológico. No vamos a dejar de insistir hasta que se adopten medidas que permitan afrontar esta situación», señala la entidad.
Además, considera que la prioridad ahora es «tomar decisiones antes de que las reservas se agoten completamente». Al mismo tiempo, reclama avanzar en un plan específico de adaptación del sector ecológico gallego a la sequía y a los episodios de calor extremo.

deduped_items.title: IRMCT judge begins investigation into circumstances of Ratko Mladic’s death
deduped_items.summary: International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) Judge Iain Bonomy has arrived in The Hague and begun an investigation into the circums
deduped_items.body_text:
IRMCT judge begins investigation into circumstances of Ratko Mladicâs death
International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) Judge Iain Bonomy has arrived in The Hague and begun an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, the Mechanism said Sunday.
Oglas
Bonomy visited the United Nations Detention Unit and the prison hospital where Mladic had been receiving treatment on Saturday, according to the IRMCT.
The investigation remains ongoing, while details are being kept confidential at this stage.
The Mechanism said it remained in regular contact with Mladicâs family, including regarding arrangements for the transfer of his remains.
Dutch authorities confirmed on Saturday that they would not open a criminal investigation into Mladicâs death and that no autopsy would be conducted.
Mladic, the former commander of the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS), died on August 27 in a detention hospital in Scheveningen while serving a life sentence.
He had been in the custody of the UN tribunal system since his arrest in Serbia in 2011, following nearly 16 years on the run.
The former Bosnian Serb military commander was sentenced to life imprisonment after being convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, crimes against humanity and violations of the laws or customs of war committed during the 1992-1995 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Mladic was convicted of genocide for the July 1995 Srebrenica massacre, in which more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys were killed.
He was also convicted over the campaign of sniping and shelling against civilians during the siege of Sarajevo, persecution and other crimes committed across Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as the taking of UN personnel hostage.
The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) convicted Mladic in 2017. His life sentence was upheld on appeal by the IRMCT in 2021.

deduped_items.title: Gervalla: Kosovo will not sacrifice rule of law to appease EU
deduped_items.summary: Kosovo’s acting Justice Minister Donika Gervalla has rejected European Union criticism of a decision concerning Kosovo Serb judges who resigned in 202
deduped_items.body_text:
Gervalla: Kosovo will not sacrifice rule of law to appease EU
Kosovoâs acting Justice Minister Donika Gervalla has rejected European Union criticism of a decision concerning Kosovo Serb judges who resigned in 2022, saying Kosovo would not sacrifice the rule of law for what she described as an EU âpolicy of appeasementâ.
Gervalla was responding to an EU statement expressing deep regret over the Kosovo Judicial Councilâs (KJC) decision to accept the resignations of Kosovo Serb judges even though they had withdrawn them.
The EU said the decision appeared incompatible with Kosovo law, due process and overall rule of law requirements and called for conditions to be created for the reintegration of Kosovo Serb judicial personnel.
Brussels also stressed that Kosovo is constitutionally a multi-ethnic society and that its justice system must reflect its ethnic diversity.
In a Facebook post, Gervalla said she could not remain silent over what she described as attempts to challenge the implementation of Kosovo law by independent institutions or impose political interpretations and preferences on them.
She argued that the KJC decision was fully in line with Kosovoâs Constitution and legislation.
âThe Law on the Kosovo Judicial Council, in Article 26, explicitly establishes the Councilâs obligation, in the event of the resignation of a judge or prosecutor, to submit a proposal for dismissal from office to the president,â Gervalla wrote.
âThese resignations were submitted in 2022. Almost four years have passed. The judges in question have not performed their duties for approximately four years.â
âTell us which law was violatedâ
Gervalla challenged those who claim the decision was contrary to Kosovo law to identify the specific legal provision that had been violated.
âTell us which law was violated. Which article? Which provision?â she said.
She asked which Kosovo law allows someone to resign from a position in the judiciary, not perform that role for almost four years and then return to the same position.
Gervalla said it was unacceptable for a Judicial Council decision based, in her view, on Kosovoâs constitutional and legal framework to be questioned for political reasons.
âIt is not possible to demand that Kosovo implement the law while at the same time putting pressure on its institutions when they implement it,â she wrote.
She said Kosovoâs European partners should support the country when its institutions make decisions based on law, ânot only when the results are politically convenientâ.
Gervalla acknowledged that representation of different communities within the judiciary is a constitutional obligation, but said this could not be used to relativise the law or judicial independence.
âThe Republic of Kosovo cannot sacrifice its rule of law for the sake of an EU policy of appeasement, to the detriment of the constitutional and legal order of the Republic of Kosovo,â Gervalla said.
âIn the Republic of Kosovo, no one is above the law. Absolutely no one. No individual. No institution. And no political pressure, local or international.â

deduped_items.title: IRMCT judge begins investigation into circumstances of Ratko Mladic’s death
deduped_items.summary: International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) Judge Iain Bonomy has arrived in The Hague and begun an investigation into the circums
deduped_items.body_text:
IRMCT judge begins investigation into circumstances of Ratko Mladicâs death
International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) Judge Iain Bonomy has arrived in The Hague and begun an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, the Mechanism said Sunday.
Oglas
Bonomy visited the United Nations Detention Unit and the prison hospital where Mladic had been receiving treatment on Saturday, according to the IRMCT.
The investigation remains ongoing, while details are being kept confidential at this stage.
The Mechanism said it remained in regular contact with Mladicâs family, including regarding arrangements for the transfer of his remains.
Dutch authorities confirmed on Saturday that they would not open a criminal investigation into Mladicâs death and that no autopsy would be conducted.
Mladic, the former commander of the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS), died on August 27 in a detention hospital in Scheveningen while serving a life sentence.
He had been in the custody of the UN tribunal system since his arrest in Serbia in 2011, following nearly 16 years on the run.
The former Bosnian Serb military commander was sentenced to life imprisonment after being convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, crimes against humanity and violations of the laws or customs of war committed during the 1992-1995 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Mladic was convicted of genocide for the July 1995 Srebrenica massacre, in which more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys were killed.
He was also convicted over the campaign of sniping and shelling against civilians during the siege of Sarajevo, persecution and other crimes committed across Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as the taking of UN personnel hostage.
The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) convicted Mladic in 2017. His life sentence was upheld on appeal by the IRMCT in 2021.

deduped_items.title: IRMCT judge begins investigation into circumstances of Ratko Mladic’s death
deduped_items.summary: International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) Judge Iain Bonomy has arrived in The Hague and begun an investigation into the circums
deduped_items.body_text:
IRMCT judge begins investigation into circumstances of Ratko Mladicâs death
International Residual Mechanism for Criminal Tribunals (IRMCT) Judge Iain Bonomy has arrived in The Hague and begun an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, the Mechanism said Sunday.
Oglas
Bonomy visited the United Nations Detention Unit and the prison hospital where Mladic had been receiving treatment on Saturday, according to the IRMCT.
The investigation remains ongoing, while details are being kept confidential at this stage.
The Mechanism said it remained in regular contact with Mladicâs family, including regarding arrangements for the transfer of his remains.
Dutch authorities confirmed on Saturday that they would not open a criminal investigation into Mladicâs death and that no autopsy would be conducted.
Mladic, the former commander of the Army of Republika Srpska (VRS), died on August 27 in a detention hospital in Scheveningen while serving a life sentence.
He had been in the custody of the UN tribunal system since his arrest in Serbia in 2011, following nearly 16 years on the run.
The former Bosnian Serb military commander was sentenced to life imprisonment after being convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, crimes against humanity and violations of the laws or customs of war committed during the 1992-1995 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
Mladic was convicted of genocide for the July 1995 Srebrenica massacre, in which more than 8,000 Bosniak men and boys were killed.
He was also convicted over the campaign of sniping and shelling against civilians during the siege of Sarajevo, persecution and other crimes committed across Bosnia and Herzegovina, as well as the taking of UN personnel hostage.
The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) convicted Mladic in 2017. His life sentence was upheld on appeal by the IRMCT in 2021.

In an interview with BIRN, one of his accusers recalls his captivity in a rat-infested pit, blindfolded and bound, fearing for his life.

deduped_items.title: EU Acknowledges Concerns Over Asbestos Contamination
deduped_items.summary: The European Commission acknowledges the seriousness of concerns over asbestos contamination in Hungary, the head of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Environment informed Laurie Kazan-Allen, coordinator of an international organization advocating an asbestos ban. The letter was forwarded to MTI on Thursday by Dániel Holdosi, an activist from Szombathely. François Wakenhut was responding to an open […] The post EU Acknowledges Concerns Over Asbestos Contamination appeared first o
deduped_items.body_text:
Temporary chemical measures on affected roads must not distract from the fact that the government still lacks a genuine and transparent action plan.Continue reading
The European Commission acknowledges the seriousness of concerns over asbestos contamination in Hungary, the head of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Environment informed Laurie Kazan-Allen, coordinator of an international organization advocating an asbestos ban. The letter was forwarded to MTI on Thursday by Dániel Holdosi, an activist from Szombathely.
François Wakenhut was responding to an open letter written in early July by 14 international anti-asbestos occupational safety, health, and environmental protection organizations and experts to the leaders of the European Union and Hungary.
In the document, they drew attention to the gravity of the situation in Szombathely, highlighting the dangers posed by the contamination, posing a particular threat to children’s health.
In a letter written on behalf of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, the director-general emphasized that it is primarily the responsibility of the competent national authorities to ensure compliance with applicable EU rules in such cases, to assess the risks, and to take the necessary protective and remediation measures.
The European Commission is confident that the national authorities will continue to act swiftly and decisively to protect public health in the affected areas,”
François Wakenhut stated.
The asbestos contamination scandal broke out the day after Hungary’s parliamentary elections, when in Vas County the head of the environmental protection department at the local government office and the mayor of Szombathely announced at an emergency press conference that, in one of the city’s single-family residential areas, on several streets of the “Oladi Plateau,” crushed stone containing asbestos had been spread years earlier. Airborne asbestos fibers are seriously harmful to health.
István Orbán, director general of the government office, said that, according to reports, four quarries in Burgenland, Austria, had previously been closed due to high asbestos content, and they suspect the material may have come from there.
András Nemény, mayor of Szombathely, announced that 12 kilometers of streets in that part of the city are covered with asbestos-contaminated crushed stone, and the cost of safely removing and disposing of it exceeds the city’s financial resources.
To access the force majeure fund, he appealed to both the outgoing government and the incoming government for assistance. Tibor Navracsics, the outgoing Minister of Regional Development, promised to make the fund available, and a supporting government resolution was passed, but only the local government was able to take concrete steps; to prevent dust from spreading, they began regularly watering the affected streets and even applied a layer of bitumen to some sections, while awaiting guidance from experts on exactly what steps to take.
In the following weeks, several municipalities in Vas County—including Kőszeg, Lukácsháza, Bük, and Sárvár—reported that they might also be affected; laboratory tests revealed asbestos levels exceeding the threshold in all of these locations.
In Táplánszentkereszt, the areas in front of the daycare center, kindergarten, and school were inadvertently covered with asbestos-containing material; there, too, the local government had no other option but to spray the area with calcium chloride. In Bük, the local government had the material removed at its own expense, in compliance with regulations governing hazardous materials.
In Szombathely, weekly public forums were held; construction in the area was halted due to the imposed restrictions, and heavy vehicle traffic was temporarily banned and then restricted during certain periods.
On May 21, the Hungarian prime minister held talks in Vienna with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker.
They announced that a joint Hungarian

deduped_items.title: Kémtávcsőnek készült, most hajtogatható tükrökkel készíthet soha nem látott méretű képeket az űrben
deduped_items.summary: A hamarosan útnak induló Roman űrteleszkóp fő tükre ugyan csak akkora, mint a Hubble-é, de százszor nagyobb területre lát rá, a csillagok fényét is ki tudja takarni, és segíthet jobban megérteni a sötét anyagot és a sötét energiát. Az egyik fő műszerét tervező csapat magyar tagjával beszélgettünk az új űrtávcső jelentőségéről. Azt is elmondta, milyen magyar sajátosság jött jól a fejlesztés során.

deduped_items.body_text:
Foreign Pupils on the Rise in Czech Schools - Nearly One in Five in Prague
Prague Morning
Of the nearly one million pupils attending Czech primary schools last academic year, almost 8% were foreign nationals, most commonly from Ukraine.
According to the Czech Statistical Office (CSO), Prague recorded the highest proportion, with foreign pupils making up 18% of all children in its primary schools.
Compulsory education is mandatory for Czech citizens as well as citizens of other European Union member states who reside in the Czech Republic for more than 90 days. The requirement also applies to foreign nationals with long-term residence permits.
Their children therefore have the same rights as Czech children, including access to free education, school meals and extracurricular activities.
The number of foreign pupils increased significantly after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, nearly doubling that year. Their numbers have continued to rise ever since. Today, children from Ukraine account for 5% of all pupils in the Czech Republic.
The trend is similar in secondary schools, where the proportion of foreign pupils reached its highest level in the past 10 years, at almost 5% of the total.
Although the number of children in primary schools has remained relatively stable at just over one million in recent years, a sharp decline is expected in the coming years due to the falling birth rate, according to Vendula Kašparová of the CSO’s Social Development Statistics Department. The office said the birth rate has been falling continuously for the fifth consecutive year.
The decline is already visible at the kindergarten level. The number of children enrolled in kindergartens fell below 350,000 in the 2025/2026 academic year, the first time this has happened since 2013. Over the past three years, enrolment has dropped by more than 21,000 children, or around 5.8%.
Fewer Children Receiving Deferrals From Starting School
Kašparová identifies another clear trend: fewer children are being granted deferrals from starting compulsory school. Since the 2021/2022 academic year, the proportion of six-year-olds whose school entry was deferred has fallen from 24.1% in September 2021 to 17.7% in September 2025, representing just under 21,000 pupils.
Furthermore, an amendment to the Education Act is expected to reduce the number of deferrals even further. Under the new rules, deferrals will only be granted when justified by a medical condition that prevents a child from attending school.
This could include a serious medical condition following surgery, cancer treatment or a moderate intellectual disability.

deduped_items.body_text:
Czechia, the Land of Burgers. More Fast Food Chains Enter the Market
Prague Morning
The Czech fast food market is expanding beyond its established players, with new international brands entering the country and existing chains opening restaurants in smaller cities.
McDonald’s and KFC continue to build their networks, while brands from Germany, the United States and Poland are looking for opportunities in the Czech Republic.
The expansion is increasingly moving beyond Prague and other major cities, with retail parks becoming an important location for new restaurants.
Burgermeister prepares Czech debut
One of the newest international brands preparing to enter the Czech market is Germany’s Burgermeister. The Berlin-based burger chain plans to open its first restaurant on Wenceslas Square at the beginning of next year.
The company already sees its Prague location as more than a single restaurant. It is also considering further locations across the country.
Popeyes and Burger King continue expanding
Burger King entered the Czech market 18 years ago and now operates around 70 restaurants. Popeyes arrived much later but has expanded quickly, opening 19 locations during its first three years in the country.
The companies are building a network that stretches from smaller regional towns to central Prague. In Králův Dvůr, a town of around 11,000 people, both Burger King and Popeyes operate at the Litavka Retail Park.
Popeyes is preparing additional restaurants at the Eden shopping centre and in the Budějovická area of Prague. The chain is also expanding into regional cities, with planned locations in Klatovy and Písek.
Five Guys adds another international brand
The Czech burger market gained another major international name last December when U.S. chain Five Guys opened its first Prague restaurant.
The restaurant is located in the former Máj department store on Národní Street. Five Guys is known for burgers prepared to order and a wide range of toppings, allowing customers to customise their meals.
Its prices, however, are generally higher than those of traditional fast food chains.
Another U.S. brand, Dave’s Hot Chicken, is also expected to enter the Czech market this year, according to consulting firm Cushman & Wakefield.
The chain specialises in spicy fried chicken and will therefore compete directly with established players such as KFC and Popeyes.
Czech chains are looking beyond their home cities
The expansion is not limited to international companies.
Czech burger chain Mama’s Burger is also developing its network. Originally based in Ostrava, the company has expanded into several larger Czech cities and operates a restaurant at Prague’s Arkády Pankrác shopping centre.
The company is also seeking franchise partners as it looks to increase the number of locations.

deduped_items.body_text:
Slavia Prague to Face Bayern Munich, Arsenal and Porto in Champions League
Prague Morning
Slavia Prague have learned their eight opponents for the 2026/27 UEFA Champions League league phase following Thursday’s draw in Monaco.
Slavia will play four matches at home at Eden Arena and four away.
At home, Slavia will welcome Arsenal, Aston Villa, Villarreal and Lens. Their away fixtures will take them to Bayern Munich, Porto, Fenerbahçe and Sabah Baku in Azerbaijan.
The most high-profile home fixture will be against Arsenal, the reigning Premier League champions. Slavia also faced the London club in last season’s Champions League campaign, making the return meeting at Eden Arena particularly notable.
The toughest away assignment is likely to come in Munich, where Slavia will face six-time European champions Bayern at the Allianz Arena. The team will also travel to Portugal to meet Porto and to Istanbul for a match against Fenerbahçe.
The longest trip of the league phase will be to Baku to face Azerbaijani champions Sabah, who are making their debut in the Champions League league phase.
How the Champions League league phase works
The 2026/27 competition is being played under UEFA’s new league-phase format for the third consecutive season. Instead of a traditional group stage, all 36 teams are placed in one league table.
Each club plays eight matches against eight different opponents, with two opponents drawn from each of the four seeding pots. Every team has four home and four away games.
The top eight teams in the final standings will advance directly to the round of 16. Teams finishing ninth to 24th will enter a knockout playoff for the remaining eight places, while clubs finishing from 25th to 36th will be eliminated.
The league phase begins on September 8–10, with six rounds taking place before the end of 2026. The final two matchdays will be played in January, with the league phase concluding on January 27. UEFA will announce the exact dates and kick-off times for each individual match later.

deduped_items.body_text:
Foreign Pupils on the Rise in Czech Schools - Nearly One in Five in Prague
Prague Morning
Of the nearly one million pupils attending Czech primary schools last academic year, almost 8% were foreign nationals, most commonly from Ukraine.
According to the Czech Statistical Office (CSO), Prague recorded the highest proportion, with foreign pupils making up 18% of all children in its primary schools.
Compulsory education is mandatory for Czech citizens as well as citizens of other European Union member states who reside in the Czech Republic for more than 90 days. The requirement also applies to foreign nationals with long-term residence permits.
Their children therefore have the same rights as Czech children, including access to free education, school meals and extracurricular activities.
The number of foreign pupils increased significantly after Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, nearly doubling that year. Their numbers have continued to rise ever since. Today, children from Ukraine account for 5% of all pupils in the Czech Republic.
The trend is similar in secondary schools, where the proportion of foreign pupils reached its highest level in the past 10 years, at almost 5% of the total.
Although the number of children in primary schools has remained relatively stable at just over one million in recent years, a sharp decline is expected in the coming years due to the falling birth rate, according to Vendula Kašparová of the CSO’s Social Development Statistics Department. The office said the birth rate has been falling continuously for the fifth consecutive year.
The decline is already visible at the kindergarten level. The number of children enrolled in kindergartens fell below 350,000 in the 2025/2026 academic year, the first time this has happened since 2013. Over the past three years, enrolment has dropped by more than 21,000 children, or around 5.8%.
Fewer Children Receiving Deferrals From Starting School
Kašparová identifies another clear trend: fewer children are being granted deferrals from starting compulsory school. Since the 2021/2022 academic year, the proportion of six-year-olds whose school entry was deferred has fallen from 24.1% in September 2021 to 17.7% in September 2025, representing just under 21,000 pupils.
Furthermore, an amendment to the Education Act is expected to reduce the number of deferrals even further. Under the new rules, deferrals will only be granted when justified by a medical condition that prevents a child from attending school.
This could include a serious medical condition following surgery, cancer treatment or a moderate intellectual disability.

deduped_items.body_text:
Midnight blaze hits Mabolo warehouse; damage reaches P1.4M
CEBU CITY, Philippines — A fire broke out shortly after midnight on Wednesday, gutting a hardware warehouse along St. Jude Street in Barangay Mabolo, Cebu City.
Fire authorities estimated the damage caused by the fire at P1.4 million.
Ronieglen Lopez, a 20-year-old mechanic at the warehouse, said he noticed smoke coming from inside the building at around 11 p.m. on Tuesday, August 25.
READ: Morning fire razes Minglanilla Public Market
Lopez lives in a company-provided workers’ housing facility adjacent to the warehouse.
“Pag-abli nako sa bintana, didto nako nakita nga nagbaga na. Mao to nibaba ko kay nagkuha og tubig kay abi namo nga matabang ra namo pero wala na jud. Mao to namukaw nalang ko sa akong mga kauban,” he said.
READ: Cebu City fires: 9 families, dozens affected in Apas, Bacayan
(When I opened the window, I saw that the fire was already blazing. So I went downstairs to get some water because we thought we could still put it out, but we really couldn’t anymore. So I just woke up my companions.)
The fire was reported to authorities shortly after midnight.
The first alarm was raised at 1:06 a.m. as flames rapidly spread through materials stored inside the facility. The fire was placed under control at 1:14 a.m. and declared out at 1:24 a.m.
As of this posting, fire investigators are continuing to determine the cause of the fire.

deduped_items.title: Subsidy removal repositioned Nigeria’s economy — Ex-Osun lawmaker
deduped_items.summary: A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress in Osun State, Olatunbosun Oyintiloye, has said that President Bola Tinubu’s removal of fuel subsidy was a bold and strategic economic reform that repositioned the country for sustainable growth and recovery. The ex-lawmaker subsequently warned those seeking political posts in the 2027 general elections against deliberate distortion of Read More: https://punchng.com/subsidy-removal-repositioned-nigerias-economy-ex-osun-lawmaker/
deduped_items.body_text:
A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress in Osun State, Olatunbosun Oyintiloye, has said that President Bola Tinubu’s removal of fuel subsidy was a bold and strategic economic reform that repositioned the country for sustainable growth and recovery.
The ex-lawmaker subsequently warned those seeking political posts in the 2027 general elections against deliberate distortion of facts regarding fuel subsidy removal.
He declared that Nigerians already realised the necessity of removing the subsidy after the bold step taken by Tinubu to end the subsidy regime.
Oyintiloye stated this in a statement obtained in Osogbo on Sunday, where he noted that the subsidy regime had imposed a huge financial burden on the country.
The former member representing Obokun State Constituency in the Osun State House of Assembly further said the reform was necessary because Nigeria could no longer sustainably spend trillions of naira subsidising petrol consumption while simultaneously grappling with fiscal pressures and development deficits.
He added that the policy should be viewed beyond the immediate increase in petrol prices and understood as an attempt to correct a long-standing structural distortion in the economy.
“The decision was difficult, but Nigeria needed the courage to confront a system that had become increasingly expensive to sustain. We cannot continue to spend trillions of naira on subsidy while critical sectors of the economy remain underfunded.
“The resources must be redirected towards development and productive investment, and that was what President Tinubu did. We are now seeing the gains,” he said.
The APC chieftain said the removal of subsidy had offered several economic benefits, including reducing the government’s fiscal burden, improving budgetary discipline and freeing resources for development.
Oyintiloye also said the reform had strengthened the economic incentive for investment in domestic refining and the downstream petroleum sector.
He cited the 650,000-barrel-per-day Dangote Refinery as an important development in Nigeria’s drive to expand local refining capacity and reduce dependence on imported refined petroleum products.
He, however, acknowledged that the policy had imposed significant short-term pressure on Nigerians, particularly through higher transportation and living costs.
“We acknowledge the hardship Nigerians are experiencing, but returning to the old system without addressing its fundamental problems would only postpone the crisis. The answer is to ensure that the resources freed from subsidy are converted into tangible benefits for the people, and the Tinubu administration has been doing that,” he said.
He urged the Federal Government to continue to prioritise investments in infrastructure, mass transportation, healthcare, education, agriculture, social protection and employment-generating activities.
He stressed that the ultimate justification for subsidy removal would be measured by its impact on the productive capacity and welfare of Nigerians.
“Nigeria must move from subsidising consumption to investing in production, creating opportunities and building an economy capable of delivering sustainable prosperity,” he said.
deduped_items.normalised_title: subsidy removal repositioned nigerias economy

deduped_items.body_text:
Islamabad and Riyadh have agreed to boost Pakistani agricultural and food exports to Saudi Arabia up to $3 billion, the countries said in a joint statement on Sunday.
The statement, shared by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), said the agreement was reached after “successful” talks between Saudi Arabia’s agriculture ministry and Pakistan’s food security ministry, at the initiative of PM Shehbaz Sharif.
At the invitation of the Pakistani government, a Saudi delegation led by Minister of Environment, Water and Agriculture Engineer Abdulrahman Al-Fadley visited Islamabad from August 26 to August 28.
The delegation included senior officials from Riyadh’s Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture, the General Food Security Authority and other relevant institutions.
PM Shehbaz met the Saudi delegation and discussed potential areas of cooperation in detail, the joint statement said, referring to Friday’s meeting.
“The two countries expressed their shared commitment to increase Pakistan’s agricultural and food exports to Saudi Arabia to $3bn, with efforts to be made to achieve the target over the next two years,” it read.
“For this purpose, rice, red meat, fruits and their concentrates, green fodder and water-efficient agricultural technologies were identified as priority sectors in collaboration with the Saudi private sector.”
During the visit, the two sides held briefings on the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia Agriculture and Food Strategic Plan and meetings with the Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC), Fauji Foundation and the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia Agri-Business Forum.
The Saudi delegation also visited the National Agricultural Research Centre (NARC).
Reaffirming their deep and historic ties, the two sides highlighted the strong alignment between Saudi Arabia’s food security priorities under Vision 2030 and Pakistan’s agricultural and food export sector.
The delegations noted that Pakistan supplied around 169,000 tonnes of rice worth about $163 million to the Saudi market in 2025. The Saudi team expressed interest in further increasing bilateral rice trade in the coming years, according to the joint statement
Furthermore, the Saudi delegation expressed interest in gradually doubling imports of red meat from Pakistan, as both sides reviewed Islamabad’s annual supply of around 30,000 tonnes of red meat worth approximately $167m.
Regarding fruits and fruit concentrates, the two sides highlighted significant potential to further increase Pakistan’s share of the Saudi market. They encouraged measures to facilitate business-to-business linkages and matchmaking between the private sectors of the two countries, as well as the mutual recognition of quality certifications.
The Saudi side identified green fodder as a promising area for expanding trade and establishing long-term supply partnerships, the joint statement said.
Both countries welcomed the successful completion of the first phase of a water-efficient irrigation programme in Punjab’s Bhakkar and expressed interest in a proposed second phase targeting small farmers.
The Saudi delegation also encouraged Pakistan to join the International Dates Council, a proposal welcomed by the Pakistani side.
The two sides also reviewed investment proposals put forward by Pakistan’s private sector in livestock, agri-food processing and the rice value chain, and agreed to maintain coordination to pursue cooperation in these areas.
“Both countries reaffirmed their broader strategic partnership,” the statement read.
Pakistan also welcomed an invitation to participate in the 43rd Saudi Agriculture Exhibition, scheduled to be held in Riyadh from October 19 to 22.
Both sides expressed satisfaction with the outcomes of the visit and agreed to maintain coordination to translate the understandings reached into practical cooperation.

deduped_items.title: Cabinet to support drone bill: source
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Cabinet to support drone bill: sourceNATIONAL DEFENSE: The Executive Yuan refrained from harsh criticism after the opposition backed uncrewed vehicle bill passed, as it plans to co-sign it, sources said
  - By Chung Li-hua / Staff reporter
 The premier is to countersign a Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT)-led bill on defense self-reliance and the uncrewed vehicle industry, and include funding for it in this year’s supplemental budget, sources said yesterday. The Legislative Yuan on Thursday passed the Act on Strengthening Defense Autonomy and Developing the Unmanned Vehicles Industry (強化國防自主暨無人載具產業發展條例), providing for NT$240 billion (US$7.59 billion) over six years in principle, while allowing additional funding subject to legislative approval. The act directs the Ministry of National Defense to prioritize the procurement of domestically produced “low-cost, high-performance” uncrewed systems. It requires the central government to, in principle, earmark NT$40 billion annually for six consecutive years, using its general budget to procure uncrewed vehicles, to reinforce national defense and drive industrial growth. A soldier from the Army Special Operations Command operates drone equipment in an undated photo.Photo courtesy of the Military News Agency The Cabinet’s proposal, which requested NT$210 billion in a special budget over six years, failed to win approval. The bill, backed by the ruling Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) caucus, was rejected by the KMT and the smaller opposition Taiwan People’s Party (TPP), which together hold a legislative majority. The legislature only passed this year’s central government budget on Aug. 14. The Cabinet had originally planned to approve the supplemental budget on Thursday, but decided to delay the move by a week, because the legislature was scheduled to vote on the uncrewed vehicle bill that day, sources said. The Cabinet also planned to adjust the supplemental budget depending on the outcome of the vote, they said. The Executive Yuan wants to accelerate defense buildup and is preparing to co-sign the uncrewed vehicle bill, they said, adding that therefore, following the passage of the opposition-led version on Thursday, it refrained from harsh criticism and instead expressed deep regret and said it would “expedite the allocation of the necessary funding.” The ministry has confirmed that all items cut from the Cabinet’s NT$1.25 trillion defense special bill would be included in this year’s supplemental budget, which means funding for uncrewed vehicles would also be included, the source said. Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) is expected to make the final decision on the amount of the supplemental budget after receiving a report from the ministry this week, sources said. The Cabinet initially planned to fund uncrewed vehicles through a special budget, so no funding for the program was included in next year’s central government budget. As the budget proposal must be submitted to the legislature tomorrow, there is not enough time to revise it beforehand, sources said. Waiting until next year’s budget is passed before seeking additional funding could be too slow, they said. The Executive Yuan is expected to submit amendments to the budget at an appropriate time, so it can be reviewed alongside the main budget proposal by the legislature, they said. deduped_items.title: US supports Taiwan’s presence at Pacific forum
deduped_items.body_text:
