            US supports Taiwan’s presence at Pacific forumPRAISE: ‘Taiwan is a reliable, like-minded and democratic partner that contributes significantly to prosperity ... across the Pacific,’ the US Department of State said
  - By Su Yong-yao / Staff reporter, with CNA
 The US backed Taiwan’s continued participation in the Pacific Islands Forum (PIF) as Taiwan and associated countries sent senior delegations to the summit this week. The 55th PIF Leaders Meeting is being held from today to Friday in Koror, Palau, with presidents and high-level officials from Pacific nations including the Marshall Islands, Tuvalu, New Zealand, Australia and Fiji expected to attend. Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍) is leading a delegation to Palau, which maintains diplomatic relations with Taiwan, from Thursday last week to Thursday this week to attend events related to the leaders’ meeting and hold sideline talks. From third left, top, Japanese Ambassador to Palau Kenichi Kasahara, Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung, Palauan President Surangel Whipps Jr, Australian Ambassador to Palau Toby Sharpe, and US Charge d’Affaires to Palau Shankar Rao gesture alongside other event guests while attending the Pacific Prosperity Exhibit in Palau on Friday.Photo courtesy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs He is representing Taiwan at the opening ceremony of the PIF Leaders Meeting and is to attend the Taiwan/ROC-Pacific Islands Forum Countries Leadership Dialogue to engage in discussions with delegations from Taiwan’s Pacific allies and associated countries. The PIF Leaders Meeting last year was hosted by the Solomon Islands, which blocked partner countries including Taiwan, China and the US from attending, saying the forum was reviewing its partnership arrangements. As Palau hosts this year’s event, associated countries are sending senior delegations to attend, and Taipei, in addition to fully supporting Palau in organizing the event, has sent the delegation led by Lin. The delegation includes representatives from the Asia Taiwanese Chambers of Commerce, the Pan-Shih Council, and industry leaders from Taiwan’s energy, technology, food, construction and organic agriculture sectors to join the exchange activities. A US Department of State spokesperson in an e-mail on Friday said “[the US] strongly supports Taiwan’s continued participation in the Pacific Islands Forum, where it has been a development partner for over three decades.” “Taiwan is a reliable, like-minded and democratic partner that contributes significantly to prosperity and economic development across the Pacific,” the spokesperson said. They said that US President Donald Trump’s administration is focused on the importance of its Pacific island friends and partners, adding that US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau looks forward to participating in the forum during his third trip to the region. Landau is traveling to Palau, the Federated States of Micronesia, the Solomon Islands and Kiribati from tomorrow to Friday next week, the US Department of State said in a news release. The theme for this year’s PIF Leaders Meeting is “B.E.L.A.U. — Building Economies: Life. Action. Unity.” Separately, PIF leaders this month did not issue a joint statement protesting China’s ballistic missile test into the Pacific Ocean last month, as Nauru and Kiribati, which have close ties to Beijing, blocked it. Kiribati President Taneti Maamau pulled out of attending the meeting this year and is sending his minister of foreign affairs and immigration, stoking concerns that the event is going to be hampered by geopolitical issues. The PIF has 18 member countries, including Palau, the Marshall Islands and Tuvalu, three of Taiwan’s diplomatic allies. deduped_items.title: Low-pressure system to bring unstable weather
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            Low-pressure system to bring unstable weather
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 Taiwan is forecast to have unstable weather this week, with a low-pressure system expected to bring heavy rain to some areas, the Central Weather Administration (CWA) said yesterday. Moisture carried by southwesterly winds, combined with the low-pressure system, is expected to affect central and southern Taiwan this week, with intermittent rain possible throughout the day and heavy localized rainfall forecast in southern areas, the CWA said. Elsewhere, active convection is expected to bring afternoon showers during the week, it added. A graphic shows expected rainfall around Taiwan from today until Saturday.Photo courtesy of the Central Weather Administration The low-pressure system could lead to the development of more tropical weather systems, creating uncertainty about the weather, it said. The low-pressure system began impacting Taiwan yesterday, it said. A heavy rain advisory was issued in 15 administrative regions across the country yesterday. A heavy rain warning means rainfall of more than 80mm in 24 hours or more than 40mm in one hour, according to the CWA. Today, brief localized showers are expected in southern and eastern Taiwan, while partly cloudy to sunny skies are forecast elsewhere and afternoon showers are possible in mountainous areas south of Hsinchu County, the CWA said. From tomorrow through Wednesday, northern, eastern and southern Taiwan should see brief showers, while heavy rain is possible in mountainous areas of central and southeastern Taiwan in the afternoons, it said. On Thursday and Friday, sporadic rainfall is likely in Keelung, along the northern coast, and in southern and eastern Taiwan, with mostly cloudy skies forecast elsewhere and afternoon thunderstorms possible, it added. WeatherRisk, a Taiwanese weather forecasting page, said that a low-pressure disturbance is expected to move near Taiwan from Wednesday through Friday. It remains unclear whether the system would strengthen into a tropical depression or typhoon, but it is expected to bring more unstable weather, with rain across Taiwan and a chance of heavy downpours, it said in a post. Projections for the system’s intensity and track remain highly uncertain, it said, urging the public to keep an eye on the latest forecasts this week.

Opinion
Will US threats over Iran be the last straw for Beijing?
China’s measured stance since the Xi-Trump summit in May is reaching a tipping point as US pressure mounts
3-MIN READ3-MIN
 Listen
Zhou Xiaoming is a senior fellow at the Centre for China and Globalisation in Beijing and a former deputy representative of China’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations Office in Geneva. 
Earlier this month, when US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened sanctions against any nation continuing to purchase Iranian crude oil, he did not name China. He did not need to. China, the Islamic Republic’s largest oil customer, is squarely in Washington’s crosshairs.
The US has already unveiled new sanctions against 60 individuals, companies and vessels linked to Iranian trade, including some in mainland China and Hong Kong. Just three months after the May summit between President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump appeared to stabilise bilateral trade relations, the fragile calm is being tested again.
So far, China has signalled it will not be coerced. The stand-off sets the stage for what could be the next major rupture in an already fraught relationship.
Washington has not been idle since May. In June, the Pentagon added dozens of companies – including Alibaba, Baidu and BYD – to its list of “Chinese military companies”, a designation that can restrict these companies’ access to US capital and market. In July, it announced a 10-12.5 per cent tariff on goods from 60 economies, including China, following its Section 301 investigation into forced labour.
This was followed by a ban on imports of Chinese robots and power inverters (July) and a 15 per cent tariff on polysilicon (August). The cumulative message is clear: Washington is tightening the screws on multiple fronts, and Iran is merely the latest lever.
Beijing’s response to this onslaught has been deliberate and calibrated. Gone are the days of blanket tariff retaliation. Instead, China has preferred to hold its fire where the cost of escalation outweighs the benefits, striking back with precision when core interests are threatened.

China’s measured stance since the Xi-Trump summit in May is reaching a tipping point as US pressure mounts
3-MIN READ3-MIN
 Listen
Zhou Xiaoming is a senior fellow at the Centre for China and Globalisation in Beijing and a former deputy representative of China’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations Office in Geneva. 
Earlier this month, when US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened sanctions against any nation continuing to purchase Iranian crude oil, he did not name China. He did not need to. China, the Islamic Republic’s largest oil customer, is squarely in Washington’s crosshairs.
The US has already unveiled new sanctions against 60 individuals, companies and vessels linked to Iranian trade, including some in mainland China and Hong Kong. Just three months after the May summit between President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump appeared to stabilise bilateral trade relations, the fragile calm is being tested again.
So far, China has signalled it will not be coerced. The stand-off sets the stage for what could be the next major rupture in an already fraught relationship.
Washington has not been idle since May. In June, the Pentagon added dozens of companies – including Alibaba, Baidu and BYD – to its list of “Chinese military companies”, a designation that can restrict these companies’ access to US capital and market. In July, it announced a 10-12.5 per cent tariff on goods from 60 economies, including China, following its Section 301 investigation into forced labour.
This was followed by a ban on imports of Chinese robots and power inverters (July) and a 15 per cent tariff on polysilicon (August). The cumulative message is clear: Washington is tightening the screws on multiple fronts, and Iran is merely the latest lever.
Beijing’s response to this onslaught has been deliberate and calibrated. Gone are the days of blanket tariff retaliation. Instead, China has preferred to hold its fire where the cost of escalation outweighs the benefits, striking back with precision when core interests are threatened.

Opinion
Will US threats over Iran be the last straw for Beijing?
China’s measured stance since the Xi-Trump summit in May is reaching a tipping point as US pressure mounts
3-MIN READ3-MIN
 Listen
Zhou Xiaoming is a senior fellow at the Centre for China and Globalisation in Beijing and a former deputy representative of China’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations Office in Geneva. 
Earlier this month, when US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened sanctions against any nation continuing to purchase Iranian crude oil, he did not name China. He did not need to. China, the Islamic Republic’s largest oil customer, is squarely in Washington’s crosshairs.
The US has already unveiled new sanctions against 60 individuals, companies and vessels linked to Iranian trade, including some in mainland China and Hong Kong. Just three months after the May summit between President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump appeared to stabilise bilateral trade relations, the fragile calm is being tested again.
So far, China has signalled it will not be coerced. The stand-off sets the stage for what could be the next major rupture in an already fraught relationship.
Washington has not been idle since May. In June, the Pentagon added dozens of companies – including Alibaba, Baidu and BYD – to its list of “Chinese military companies”, a designation that can restrict these companies’ access to US capital and market. In July, it announced a 10-12.5 per cent tariff on goods from 60 economies, including China, following its Section 301 investigation into forced labour.
This was followed by a ban on imports of Chinese robots and power inverters (July) and a 15 per cent tariff on polysilicon (August). The cumulative message is clear: Washington is tightening the screws on multiple fronts, and Iran is merely the latest lever.
Beijing’s response to this onslaught has been deliberate and calibrated. Gone are the days of blanket tariff retaliation. Instead, China has preferred to hold its fire where the cost of escalation outweighs the benefits, striking back with precision when core interests are threatened.

deduped_items.title: Renee was at Gyirong Port minutes before flood struck, now her family want to travel from Australia to help search
deduped_items.summary: Missing woman’s partner and daughters fundraise to join search in one of the hardest-hit areas of Nepal Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updatesGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastClair Spry says her sister would hate the attention. She would want it focused on the Nepali people, who have been displaced or are in need of aid. She would want it to be on the impact of the climate crisis, especially on the world’s most economically vulnerable populations.“Her fo
deduped_items.body_text:
Clair Spry says her sister would hate the attention. She would want it focused on the Nepali people, who have been displaced or are in need of aid. She would want it to be on the impact of the climate crisis, especially on the world’s most economically vulnerable populations.
“Her focus right now would not be on her; it would be on the families,” Spry said. “So many people, the Nepalese people, that have been horribly displaced and traumatised. She would want the attention on them and how we are going to help them.
“And global warming. This is something the poorest people of the world are affected by. It’s not the New Yorkers, it’s the people who are in these parts of the world. For Renee, that would be heartbreaking.”
Like many of the missing Australians, Renee arrived at Gyirong Port just 10 minutes before the flood struck. The area was one of the hardest hit – images from Chinese rescue teams show the area completely flattened. Huge buildings, power lines, everything – just wiped away.
Renee is a disability support worker who lives on the Sunshine Coast. She has been with her partner, Shaun, an emergency nurse, since they were 15, and they share two daughters in their 20s.
Clair has set up a GoFundMe to get the three of them over to Nepal – Shaun wants to travel to the port to try to find any signs of her. And their daughters, Lily and Ruby, don’t want him to go alone.
“Their first reaction is, we have to go. The practicalities, and what can actually be done in the first few days, it hasn’t been possible [to enter the area], but they still want to go,” she said.
“And if they are able to find her, to bring her home.”
Renee’s family understand how dire the situation is, and how unlikely it is that she, or anyone in that same area, survived. But until they know for certain, they would hold hope, she said.
“Everyone’s very realistic. We know how bad this was and where she was. But until they find her, everyone’s got this little slither of hope that maybe she’s stuck somewhere and can’t get out, or she’s injured.
“I’ve been looking through pictures trying to identify someone or see her. But we understand the reality of this situation.”
Like most Australians, Renee had come to Nepal on a pilgrimage. Spry said her sister was a “deeply spiritual” person who loved to help people.
“She had two degrees, and she chose to do something that was … a completely selfless vocation. Her priority was always other people,” she said.
“Every person she touched, they knew her love and kindness. She would be so uncomfortable with all this.”
The family of Michael Keats, an Australian who had been near the Tibet-Nepal border when flash flooding began, confirmed his death in posts to social media on Sunday. 
 Keats’s wife, Emily Boyd, said on Instagram he had been on a pilgrimage to Mt Kailash that had been a “dream for many years”.
“Mike went on a pilgrimage to Mt Kailash seeking enlightenment,” Boyd said.
“There’s a bittersweetness knowing that there was nothing more that Mike wanted then to know God, and to merge with the divine.
 ”He was a mystic, a medicine man, a teacher, leader, partner, father, brother, son, uncle and dearly beloved friend. He showed up for so many people in so many ways. A heart of pure gold. We love you forever and always.”

deduped_items.title: Editorial: Recuperación del patrimonio con justicia social
deduped_items.summary: Esta semana se produjeron o anunciaron importantes avances en la recuperación de recursos producto de la corrupción. El presidente de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación (SCJN), Hugo Aguilar Ortiz, desechó de manera inapelable, por “improcedente”, el trámite con el que la defensa de Emilio Lozoya Austin pretendía revertir la extinción de dominio sobre la residencia valuada en 51 millones de pesos que el ex director de Pemex adquirió con parte de los 3.5 millones de dólares que recibió como
deduped_items.body_text:
sta semana se produjeron o anunciaron importantes avances en la recuperación de recursos producto de la corrupción. El presidente de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación (SCJN), Hugo Aguilar Ortiz, desechó de manera inapelable, por “improcedente”, el trámite con el que la defensa de Emilio Lozoya Austin pretendía revertir la extinción de dominio sobre la residencia valuada en 51 millones de pesos que el ex director de Pemex adquirió con parte de los 3.5 millones de dólares que recibió como soborno del empresario Alonso Ancira por la compra fraudulenta de Agronitrogenados.
Por otra parte, el gobierno federal logró la recuperación de 5.8 millones de dólares como parte de una red de corrupción encabezada por el ex secretario de Seguridad Pública, Genaro García Luna, en colaboración con la familia Weinberg. Se trata de una primera recuperación derivada de operaciones corruptas del ex funcionario que generaron afectaciones por 528 millones de pesos y 727.9 millones de dólares, según informó la Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF) de la Secretaría de Hacienda.
La misma UIF dio a conocer que en dos años de la actual administración federal ha incorporado a 2 mil 395 sujetos al grupo de personas bloqueadas por realizar presuntas operaciones bancarias ilícitas. Con ello, se han inmovilizado 24 mil 662 cuentas en el sistema financiero nacional, de las cuales 7 mil 861 corresponden a organizaciones del crimen organizado. Los recursos bloqueados involucran un monto global de 8 mil 670 millones de pesos. Además, la SCJN dictaminó que los jueces federales ya no pueden otorgar amparos para ordenar el desbloqueo total o inmediato de cuentas bancarias congeladas por la UIF. Debe recordarse que los togados abusaron de este recurso jurídico hasta el punto en que la esposa de García Luna obtuvo un amparo para mover dinero ilícito sólo un día después de que su marido fue condenado por narcotráfico.
Las acciones referidas representan una ínfima parte de los perjuicios causados a la nación por ex funcionarios como Lozoya Austin y García Luna. Así, los alrededor de 3 millones de dólares de la mansión incautada en la colonia Lomas de Bezares palidecen frente a los 275 millones de dólares (4 mil 684 millones de pesos, al cambio actual) que Pemex entregó a Ancira por una planta inservible por culpa de las gestiones inescrupulosas y antinacionales de Lozoya. Asimismo, los 5 millones de dólares de la fortuna mal habida de García Luna son muy poco frente a los cientos de millones que saqueó del Estado mexicano, gracias a los favores políticos que obtuvo durante el calderonato y el peñato.
Con todo, los esfuerzos de las autoridades y los primeros frutos que han rendido tienen el valor de marcar un cambio de época con respecto al paradigma neoliberal en el que la transferencia de bienes públicos a manos privadas, los negocios a expensas del Estado y el tráfico de influencias eran premiados como señales de éxito, y la impunidad estaba codificada en las leyes y en códigos cupulares mafiosos. Además, cabe destacar que la recuperación del patrimonio nacional se realiza con sentido de justicia social, como muestra la decisión de destinar los 5.8 millones de dólares de la red de corrupción de García Luna a ampliar la infraestructura educativa del nivel medio superior en la Montaña de Guerrero, una de las regiones con mayores rezagos del país.

Por otra parte, el gobierno federal logró la recuperación de 5.8 millones de dólares como parte de una red de corrupción encabezada por el ex secretario de Seguridad Pública, Genaro García Luna, en colaboración con la familia Weinberg. sta semana se produjeron o anunciaron importantes avances en la recuperación de recursos producto de la corrupción. El presidente de la Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación (SCJN), Hugo Aguilar Ortiz, desechó de manera inapelable, por “improcedente”, el trámite con el que la defensa de Emilio Lozoya Austin pretendía revertir la extinción de dominio sobre la residencia valuada en 51 millones de pesos que el ex director de Pemex adquirió con parte de los 3.5 millones de dólares que recibió como soborno del empresario Alonso Ancira por la compra fraudulenta de Agronitrogenados.
Por otra parte, el gobierno federal logró la recuperación de 5.8 millones de dólares como parte de una red de corrupción encabezada por el ex secretario de Seguridad Pública, Genaro García Luna, en colaboración con la familia Weinberg. Se trata de una primera recuperación derivada de operaciones corruptas del ex funcionario que generaron afectaciones por 528 millones de pesos y 727.9 millones de dólares, según informó la Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF) de la Secretaría de Hacienda.
La misma UIF dio a conocer que en dos años de la actual administración federal ha incorporado a 2 mil 395 sujetos al grupo de personas bloqueadas por realizar presuntas operaciones bancarias ilícitas. Con ello, se han inmovilizado 24 mil 662 cuentas en el sistema financiero nacional, de las cuales 7 mil 861 corresponden a organizaciones del crimen organizado. Los recursos bloqueados involucran un monto global de 8 mil 670 millones de pesos. Además, la SCJN dictaminó que los jueces federales ya no pueden otorgar amparos para ordenar el desbloqueo total o inmediato de cuentas bancarias congeladas por la UIF. Debe recordarse que los togados abusaron de este recurso jurídico hasta el punto en que la esposa de García Luna obtuvo un amparo para mover dinero ilícito sólo un día después de que su marido fue condenado por narcotráfico.
Las acciones referidas representan una ínfima parte de los perjuicios causados a la nación por ex funcionarios como Lozoya Austin y García Luna. Así, los alrededor de 3 millones de dólares de la mansión incautada en la colonia Lomas de Bezares palidecen frente a los 275 millones de dólares (4 mil 684 millones de pesos, al cambio actual) que Pemex entregó a Ancira por una planta inservible por culpa de las gestiones inescrupulosas y antinacionales de Lozoya. Asimismo, los 5 millones de dólares de la fortuna mal habida de García Luna son muy poco frente a los cientos de millones que saqueó del Estado mexicano, gracias a los favores políticos que obtuvo durante el calderonato y el peñato.
Con todo, los esfuerzos de las autoridades y los primeros frutos que han rendido tienen el valor de marcar un cambio de época con respecto al paradigma neoliberal en el que la transferencia de bienes públicos a manos privadas, los negocios a expensas del Estado y el tráfico de influencias eran premiados como señales de éxito, y la impunidad estaba codificada en las leyes y en códigos cupulares mafiosos. Además, cabe destacar que la recuperación del patrimonio nacional se realiza con sentido de justicia social, como muestra la decisión de destinar los 5.8 millones de dólares de la red de corrupción de García Luna a ampliar la infraestructura educativa del nivel medio superior en la Montaña de Guerrero, una de las regiones con mayores rezagos del país.

Debe recordarse que los togados abusaron de este recurso jurídico hasta el punto en que la esposa de García Luna obtuvo un amparo para mover dinero ilícito sólo un día después de que su marido fue condenado por narcotráfico.
Las acciones referidas representan una ínfima parte de los perjuicios causados a la nación por ex funcionarios como Lozoya Austin y García Luna. Así, los alrededor de 3 millones de dólares de la mansión incautada en la colonia Lomas de Bezares palidecen frente a los 275 millones de dólares (4 mil 684 millones de pesos, al cambio actual) que Pemex entregó a Ancira por una planta inservible por culpa de las gestiones inescrupulosas y antinacionales de Lozoya. Asimismo, los 5 millones de dólares de la fortuna mal habida de García Luna son muy poco frente a los cientos de millones que saqueó del Estado mexicano, gracias a los favores políticos que obtuvo durante el calderonato y el peñato.
Con todo, los esfuerzos de las autoridades y los primeros frutos que han rendido tienen el valor de marcar un cambio de época con respecto al paradigma neoliberal en el que la transferencia de bienes públicos a manos privadas, los negocios a expensas del Estado y el tráfico de influencias eran premiados como señales de éxito, y la impunidad estaba codificada en las leyes y en códigos cupulares mafiosos. Además, cabe destacar que la recuperación del patrimonio nacional se realiza con sentido de justicia social, como muestra la decisión de destinar los 5.8 millones de dólares de la red de corrupción de García Luna a ampliar la infraestructura educativa del nivel medio superior en la Montaña de Guerrero, una de las regiones con mayores rezagos del país.

deduped_items.title: Santiago Loza y el viaje como espejo: “Diario chino” y “Los días chinos”, dos caras de una experiencia
deduped_items.summary: Después de años de postergar el viaje, Santiago Loza llegó a China con una cámara prestada y la consigna de volver con una película. De allí surgieron un documental, un diario y una obra literaria que comparten escenas, preguntas y materiales. El escritor y cineasta convierte el desplazamiento en una forma de pensar sobre la escritura, los vínculos y sí mismo.

Pueblos destruidos, cientos de personas enterradas y riesgo de inundaciones: así se vive la tragedia de Nepal tras avalancha; ‘Todo quedó devastado’
La tragedia deja hasta el momento deja cerca de 700 muertos y más de 3.000 desaparecidos. EL TIEMPO habló con una sobreviviente de la tragedia.
Era una mañana soleada para Dikshya Subedi, de 28 años, en Katmandú, la capital de Nepal. Mientras hablaba por teléfono con su tía, que vive en Devighat, una pequeña localidad a orillas del río Trishuli, a unos 60 kilómetros de la capital, las imágenes que aparecían en televisión le hicieron temer lo peor: un torrente de agua y lodo arrasaba con todo a su paso en la zona donde vivía su familia.
A salvo, pero impotente y sin creer aún que el pueblo de su familia estuviera en la ruta de destrucción, Dikshya volvió a comunicarse con su tía y preguntó: “¿Están todos bien?”. Una voz, débil y sollozante, respondió: “No hay nada. Todo está destruido”.
“No llegó ninguna alerta, no hubo señales, ni siquiera estaba lloviendo. En unos 15 minutos, todo quedó devastado”, relata Dikshya a EL TIEMPO al recordar aquel momento que, desde el miércoles, persigue a cientos de miles de familias en la frontera entre Nepal y China.
Esa mañana, según concluyó el Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos, un enorme glaciar del macizo deLangtang, a 5.200 metros de altitud, se desprendió y cayó más de 1.000 metros sobre la cuenca del ríoLhendeKhola, provocando una avalancha de hielo, lodo, rocas y sedimento que recorrió unos 20 kilómetros en apenas siete minutos, provocando crecidas de ríos y destrucción de aldeas y puentes río abajo por el valle deRasuwa.
Siempre trataba de ayudar cuando ocurrían estos desastres. Pero cuando le pasa a tu propia familia, es desgarrador
La caída del glaciar fue tan poderosa que desencadenó una señal sísmica de magnitud 5,2. Científicos del Centro Internacional para el Desarrollo Integrado de las Montañas (ICIMOD) registraron además un aumento del caudal de hasta nueve metros en solo 30 minutos en partes del ríoTrishuli.
La tragedia deja un desenlace -aún preliminar- de 682 fallecidos -675 en Nepal y siete en China-, así como más de 3.000 personas desaparecidas en am

deduped_items.body_text:
“It’s Very Likely That a Different Party System Will Emerge in Venezuela”
Prof. Guillermo Aveledo Coll discusses the unfolding negotiations, the future of political parties, and the lessons Rómulo Betancourt might offer Machado
The trajectory of the political transition that many Venezuelans await since January 3 seems to have been clarifying over the past few weeks. The first expected milestone is the reform of the Supreme Court of Justice, although it remains to be seen how many of the new magistrates will be independent and how many tied to factions of the chavista elite. The expectation is that, before the end of the year, the agenda will include a new board of rectors for the CNE and the long-awaited electoral calendar. In Panama, María Corina Machado had opened to negotiating these matters directly with Delcy Rodríguez, but the United States decided to manage the institutional opening through a small group of opposition figures, former lawmakers from Primero Justicia and Voluntad Popular in the 2015 National Assembly. The discomfort of Machado and her inner circle with this decision is no secret. The opposition leader has stated that she does not intend to stand in the way. Individuals linked to her team and party have raised doubts about the negotiation’s initial legitimacy and early progress, while other longtime opposition figures have welcomed the recent releases of political prisoners and the roadmap the US has outlined.
At Caracas Chronicles, we sat down to talk with Guillermo Aveledo Coll, a political scientist, expert in Venezuelan political history, and researcher of the ideas that have shaped its parties and conflicts. Aveledo views the unfolding dialogue favorably. He believes general elections must take place in Venezuela as soon as possible, though not without first tying up loose ends related to the broad recognition of any electoral process and the stability of future governments. He also discussed the dynamics that could emerge among political parties amid a transition, both within the anti-chavista camp and inside the chavista movement. Much like Marco Rubio in January, he made reference to the Spanish Transition. Finally, he reflected on our last transition to democracy (1958–1968) and how Rómulo Betancourt and Acción Democrática adapted to move forward in the face of adversity.
Recently, María Corina Machado used a term typical in transition frameworks. She said that the transition to democracy cannot be an elite pact made behind the people’s backs and without a popular mandate. Does the agenda unfolding between a commission of the Delcy government and the Delegated Commission of the old 2015 National Assembly fall into the category of an elite pact? You have been a defender of the legacy of the Puntofijo Pact. Is an elite pact problematic in these particular circumstances?
What we are seeing, which points embryonically toward an elite agreement, will have to be filtered through the will of the population, because the ultimate source of legitimacy in a democratic republic passes through it. The Puntofijo Pact was a concrete agreement on political rules among parties. However, had those parties lacked inherent legitimacy and a firm foothold, those rules might have overwhelmed them. In those elections, an independent candidate backed by one of the historic parties, Rear Admiral Wolfgang Larrazábal, obtained a very high percentage of the vote and came in second. So it could very well have been something that surpassed them, that swallowed them up.
Venezuela will need elections. It also needs the freedoms and guarantees for those elections to take place. Not because winning them without those guarantees is impossible, but because the opposition’s victories haven’t been recognized without them, while a government win leaves reasonable doubts regarding legitimacy. Individuals linked to her team and party have raised doubts about the negotiation’s initial legitimacy and early progress, while other longtime opposition figures have welcomed the recent releases of political prisoners and the roadmap the US has outlined.

deduped_items.title: Hong Kong’s first Chinese medicine hospital to offer inpatient services from December

deduped_items.title: Éboulement d'une décharge en Guinée: visite du président Doumbouya auprès de la population endeuillée
deduped_items.summary: Une semaine après l’éboulement meurtrier de la décharge de Dar-es-Salam, le président guinéen Mamadi Doumbouya s’est rendu samedi 29 août sur les lieux du drame. Accompagné de plusieurs membres du gouvernement, le chef de l’État est venu constater l’ampleur des dégâts, exprimer sa compassion aux familles des victimes et suivre les opérations engagées par les autorités. Cette visite intervient alors que les opérations de démolition des habitations situées aux abords de la décharge se poursuivent.

deduped_items.title: RDC: le gouvernement envisage une banque publique de l’habitat face au déficit de logements
deduped_items.summary: En République démocratique du Congo (RDC), le gouvernement souhaite s’attaquer à la problématique du logement. Face à un déficit estimé à plus de quatre millions d’unités, la Première ministre Judith Suminwa a proposé, vendredi 28 août 2026 en Conseil des ministres, de transformer le Fonds national de l’habitat (FONHAB) en une véritable banque publique dédiée au secteur. deduped_items.title: “The Strategy of Terrorism”
deduped_items.summary: A quarter century before 9/11, an upsurge in global terrorism prompted the historian David Fromkin to examine its purpose and method. Terrorism was a strategy of the weak, Fromkin wrote in these pages, but modern technology had enabled it “to enter the political arena on a new scale.” And its surprising success seemed to be due, in large part, “to a miscomprehension of the strategy by its opponents.”

deduped_items.body_text:
Haaretz: Army concerned Netanyahu escalating West Bank tensions before elections
Israeli military sources have voiced concern that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could be deliberately escalating tensions in the occupied West Bank ahead of elections, Haaretz is reporting.
The report said the violence was being used to divert attention from the failures surrounding the 7 October 2023 attack.
Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir has questioned the government’s intentions and wants to avoid drawing the army into new crises driven by political considerations, the newspaper said.
Political figures in Israel, including Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, have openly advocated a more intense campaign in the occupied West Bank that could be used to justify military action against the Palestinian Authority.
The comments by senior military officials come as Israeli settler violence against Palestinians continues to rise across the occupied territory, with Palestinians and rights groups accusing Israeli forces of providing protection or failing to intervene during attacks.

deduped_items.title: South Africa accuses Israel of violating ICJ's legally binding provisional measures
deduped_items.summary: South Africa accuses Israel of violating ICJ's legally binding provisional measures Submitted by MEE staff on Sun, 08/30/2026 - 09:58 Pretoria submits evidence to a dedicated judicial committee, arguing that the ongoing defiance of the court's mandates undermines its legitimacy Displaced Palestinians walk past tents and destroyed buildings near the beachfront in Gaza City on 14 August 2026 (AFP) Off South Africa has accused Israel of breaking legally binding orders issued by the International Co
deduped_items.body_text:
South Africa accuses Israel of violating ICJ's legally binding provisional measures
South Africa has accused Israel of breaking legally binding orders issued by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) intended to protect Palestinians in Gaza, while calling on the international community "to take all necessary action to prevent and punish genocide".
In a statement issued by the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO), Pretoria said that Israel has refused to comply with three separate provisional measure orders issued by the ICJ. This refusal "undermines their protective function and entails further destruction of the Palestinian group", the statement says.
"The Provisional Measures were not only ordered to protect the rights of the Palestinian people under the Genocide Convention, they also safeguard the administration of justice and the legitimacy of the ICJ itself, by ensuring that the rights the Court is called upon to vindicate are not destroyed before it renders its final decision."
The statement added: "The Court’s orders are binding on Israel, and the international community also has an obligation to protect the Palestinian people from genocide, including to take all necessary action to prevent and punish genocide."
Earlier this week, the South African government submitted a dossier of evidence to a dedicated committee of judges tasked with monitoring the court’s provisional measures.

Issued in 2024, the three provisional orders issued by the ICJ against Israel include the prevention of genocidal acts and incitement, ceasing military operations in Rafah and providing immediate access for Palestinians to humanitarian assistance and basic services in the Gaza Strip.
The provisional orders also mandated Israel to submit formal reports to the court detailing steps it has taken to comply, which it did in February 2024.
Under Article 11 of the ICJ’s Internal Judicial Practice, the committee examines information supplied by parties and recommends potential options to the broader court.
The South African government emphasised that the measures "safeguard the administration of justice and the legitimacy of the ICJ itself, by ensuring that the rights the Court is called upon to vindicate are not destroyed before it renders its final decision".
Pretoria’s dossier highlights the ongoing humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Gaza, noting that as of August 2026, at least 73,407 Palestinians have been killed and 174,335 others wounded since 7 October 2023, representing more than 10 percent of Gaza’s entire population.
Among the survivors, an estimated 46,000 Palestinians, including children, are living with severe conflict-related conditions such as amputations and traumatic brain and spinal cord injuries.
The submission also notes that since the announcement of a ceasefire, the Israeli military has continued to kill an average of one Palestinian child every day and that the trauma and unbearable living conditions in Gaza's ever-shrinking territorial enclaves have caused Palestinian miscarriage rates to increase more than three-fold in 2026.
Palestinian rights organisation Al-Haq has welcomed South Africa’s submission to the ICJ documenting Israel’s non-compliance with the provisional orders.
"As the genocide continues, we call on the Court to act propio motu, including through additional Provisional Measures Orders," the organisation said.
Erasing the record
South Africa’s government emphasised that the ICJ’s orders are strictly binding and that the international community bears a collective obligation to take all necessary action to prevent and punish genocide.
"For almost three years, Israel has bombarded Gaza, killing and maiming tens of thousands of children, men and women," the DIRCO statement reads.

deduped_items.summary: As the succession to António Guterres looms, Africa can no longer be reduced to its 54 votes. deduped_items.title: غرق قارب ركاب يقل 270 قبالة سواحل قبرص
deduped_items.summary: أفادت وسائل إعلام في منطقة القبارصة الأتراك ​بأن ‌قارب ركاب على متنه حوالي 270 ‌شخصا انقلب قبالة سواحل شمال قبرص اليوم الأحد، وأن عمليات البحث والإنقاذ ​جارية. وقال مراد شنكول ‌رئيس بلدية كيرينيا لمحطة (سي.إن.إن ترك) إن فرق ‌الإنقاذ وصلت إلى 159 ​راكبا من أصل 258 كانوا على متن القارب. وذكرت ​صحيفة كيبريس أن ​القارب بدأ ​في الامتلاء بالمياه على بعد نحو ​أربعة أميال من الشاطئ. وأضافت الصحيفة أنه جرى الدفع بسيارات إسعاف إلى الموقع.

deduped_items.title: Roseline Hamel and Nassera Kermiche: Beyond sorrow
deduped_items.summary: On the sidelines of the 2026 Rimini Meeting for Friendship Among Peoples, Roseline Hamel and Nassera Kermiche, who have come to be known as “sisters in sorrow", speak to Vatican News about the tragedy that unites them. Roseline is the sister of Fr Jacques Hamel, the French priest who was killed while celebrating Mass in a terrorist attack in 2016. Nassera is the mother of one of the two teenagers who perpetrated the attack and was subsequently shot dead by police. Read all

Nassera is the mother of one of the two teenagers who perpetrated the attack and was subsequently shot dead by police. Read all

deduped_items.title: CIA and Vatican visits converge in Moscow amid rising tensions over Ukraine
deduped_items.summary: VATICAN CITY (RNS) — As the CIA director quietly carried warnings to Moscow, Pope Leo’s foreign minister arrived offering dialogue and humanitarian cooperation — two contrasting missions that one Vatican expert likened to a 'good cop, bad cop operation.'
